subject: Convert intro to technical discovery + availability check
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Lee <harper.lee@everledger.com>
Cc: Eng Ops <eng-ops@everledger.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Convert intro to technical discovery + availability check

Hi Harper —

Thanks again for signing up for a demo. Given the use case you described in the intake form (heavy embedding/streaming, multi-tenant data isolation), I wanted to propose converting the scheduled 30-minute intro demo into a 90-minute technical discovery / scoping workshop so we can: 

- Walk through your data flow and security constraints
- Validate latency and throughput expectations against our serving profiles
- Draft a lightweight mutual action plan (POC scope, success criteria, next steps)

Are you open to switching formats? If so, we have these windows next week (all times PDT):
- Tue May 11: 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed May 12: 09:00–10:30 or 13:00–14:30

If those don't work, please share a couple of 90-minute windows the week of May 17 and we will align internal participants (solutions engineer + infra). I'm attaching a draft agenda and a short prework checklist — nothing heavy, just a couple of artifact requests to make the session actionable.

Quick ask: please confirm which Everledger folks should join from engineering/security so we make sure the right people are on the call.

Thanks,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood-technical-discovery-agenda.pdf (PDF preview), customer-prework-checklist.md (text)
From: Harper Lee <harper.lee@everledger.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eng Ops <eng-ops@everledger.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Convert intro to technical discovery + availability check

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the suggestion, that actually sounds better than the intro. A few constraints from our side: 

- Our CTO (Liang Chen) is traveling May 10–14 and would like to be on any scoping session if possible.
- We prefer a slot when both an engineer who owns our embeddings pipeline (Ava R.) and a security reviewer (security@everledger.com) can attend.
- Week of May 17 looks ideal. Do you have any 90-minute slots that week?

Also, can you confirm the intended internal participants from Redwood and whether you'll cover data retention/audit logging in the agenda? Those are critical for procurement.

Best,
Harper

--
Harper Lee
Head of Product, Everledger
harper.lee@everledger.com

Marissa / Karthik —

Harper wants to move the session to the week of May 17 so their CTO can attend. Can you confirm internal availability and who should lead data/security portions? Proposed internal roster: 

- Marissa Cole (Solutions Eng) — lead workshop, architecture walkthrough
- Karthik Iyer (Field SE) — instrumentation / embeddings performance deep dive
- Sean Gallagher — AEs context and mutual action plan

Suggested slots (PDT):
- Tue May 18: 09:00–10:30 or 13:00–14:30
- Wed May 19: 10:00–11:30

Notes for the agenda: include a 15-minute security checklist segment (retention, audit logs, KMS/HSM), and confirm a short prework item for Everledger: sample tokenization schema and a short latency target doc.

Marissa — if you can't make the Tue morning slot, who from your team can step in to lead the architecture portion? Karthik — can you hold the Tue 13:00 slot as tentative? I will not finalize until Harper confirms.

Thanks,
Sean

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per availability, we've locked Tue May 18, 13:00–14:30 PDT for the 90-minute technical discovery workshop. Calendar invite sent (link below).

Final attendee list (please adjust if needed):
- Everledger: Harper Lee (Product), Liang Chen (CTO), Ava R. (Embeddings), security@everledger.com
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (Solutions Eng), Karthik Iyer (Field SE), Sean Gallagher (AE)

1) 10 min — introductions & goals
2) 25 min — architecture walkthrough (Everledger data + ingestion)
3) 30 min — model/serving feasibility & perf expectations (Karthik)

5) 10 min — mutual action plan (POC scope, success criteria, next steps)

Prework (short):
- Everledger to share a sample tokenization schema (or example dataset) and a one-paragraph latency target by EOD Fri May 14.
- Redwood to share a short agenda + meeting materials (attached).

Attachments: redwood-technical-discovery-agenda.pdf, customer-prework-checklist.md
